Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

MOSQUITO  NETS  —  SPECIFICATION 

(First  Revision  ) 


First  Reprint  DECEMBER  2000 


UDC   645.427  :  677. 072. 7327.736 


©BIS  199I 

BUREAU     OF     INDIAN     STANDARDS 

MANAK    BHAVAN,    9    BAHADUR    SHAH    ZAFAR  MARG 
NEW  DELHI  110002 

January  1991  Price  Group  2 


Made-up  Textiles  (  Other  than  Ready-Made  Garments  )  Sectional  Committee,  TXD  20 


FOREWORD 

This  Indian  Standard  (  First  Revision  )  was  adopted  by  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  on 
10  May  1990,  after  the  draft  finalized  by  the  Made  up  Textiles  (  Other  than  Ready-Made  Garments  ) 
Sectional  Ccrrmittee  had  been  approved  by  the  Textile  Division  Council. 

The  present  revision  of  the  standard  has  been  done  mainly  for  including  the  following. 

a)  Mosquito  nets  made  out  of  HDPE  monofilament  mocquito  nettings,  round  mesh 
conforming  to  IS  10054  1981  specification  for  high  density  polyethylene  (HDPE) 
monofilament  mosquito  netting,  round  mesh*  and 

b)  Mosquito  nets  made  out  of  nylon  multifilament  mosquito  nettings. 

Opportunity  has  also  been  utilized  to  update  the  references  to  Indian  Standards  and  to  modify 
certain  other  clauses  of  the  standard  based  on  the  experience  gained  since  its  publication  in  1981 

For  the  purpose  of  deciding  whether  a  particular  requirement  of  this  standard  is  complied  with, 
the  final  value,  observed  or  calculated,  expressing  the  result  of  a  test  or  analysis,  shall  be  rounded 
off  in  accordance  with  IS  2  .  1960  'Rules  for  rounding  off  numerical  values  (revised)*  The 
number  of  significant  places  retained  in  the  rounded  off  value  should  be  the  same  as  that  of  the 
specified  value  in  this  standard

IS  9886  :  1990 


Indian  Standard 

MOSQUITO  NETS  —  SPECIFICATION 

(  First  Revision  ) 


1  SCOPE 

1.1  This  standard  prescribes  the  requirements 
of  three  types  of  mosquito  nets,  made  out  of 
cotton  mosquito  netting,  HDPE  mosquito  netting 
and  nylon  mosquito  netting  (  see  3.1  ) 

2  REFERENCES 

2.1  The  Indian  Standards  listed  in  Annex  A  are 
necessary  adjuncts  to  this  standard 

3  MATERIALS 

3.1  Nettings 

The  nettings  used  for  the  manufacture  of  three 
types  of  mosquito  nets  shall  conform  to  the 
following  Indian  Standards 

Tvpe  of  Materials  fir  Conforming  to 

Mosquito  Wall  and  Top 

Net 

1  Cotton  mosquito  net-     IS    1143     1973 
ting      square      mesh, 

bleached  or  dyed  (  as 
specified  in  the 
contract  or  order  ) 

or 
Cotton  mosquito  net-     IS     1431      1973 
ting  round  mesh,  dyed 

2  HDPE    monofilament     IS  10054    1981 
mosquito  netting, 

round  mesh 

3  Nylon   mosquito  net-     As  specified  in 
ting  contract/order 

NOTF  —  Recommended      specificitton      for     nylon 
netting  is  given  in  Annex  B  for  guidance 

3.2  The  other  materials  shall  conform  to  the 
following  Indian  Standards 

Cotton  calico,  bleached  IS  1544     1973 

or  dyed  (used  as  rein- 
forcement piece  at  the 
bottom  of  the  net  ) 

Cotton  sewing  thread  of        Variety  No  31  of 
matching  shade  IS  1720  •  1978 

Cotton  NEWAR  13  mm  IS  1895     1982 

width  (  scoured  or 
dyed  ) 

Cotton    tape     25      mm  IS  6117.  1977 

width  ( scoured  or 
dyed  ) 

4  MANUFACTURE  AND  WORKMANSHIP 

4.1  Wall  and  Top 

The  top  shall  be  made  from  one  piece  of  netting 
(  see  also  3.1  ),  as  specified  in  the  contract/ 
order 


The  walls  shall  be  made  from  one  piece  of  net- 
ting and  shall  be  closed  with  lapped  seam  and 
the  seam  shall  be  at  the  one  of  the  corners  (  see 
also  5.4  )  One  edge  of  the  netting  of  the  wall 
shall  be  attached  to  the  netting  at  the  top  by 
means  of  a  plain  seam,  reinforced  by  stitching  a 
25  mm  cotton  tape  over  it  all  round  as  shown 
in  Fig   1 

4  2  Reinforcement  at  Bottom 

The  bottom  edge  of  the  walls  shall  be  reinforced 
by  stitching  a  strip  of  cotton  calico  of  matching 
shade  with  the  netting  by  a  lapped  seam  as 
shown  in  Fig    1 

4.3  Tying  Tapes 

The  nets  shall  be  provided  with  eight  tying  tapes 
at  the  roof  and  four  tying  tapes  at  the  seam 
joining  the  bottom  reinforcing  piece,  as  shown 
in  Fig.  1 

4.4  Stitching 

The  nets  shall  be  made  with  lock  stitch  of  even 
tension  throughout  and  loose  ends  securely 
fastened  off  The  number  of  stitches  per  deci- 
metre shall  remain  within  28  to  35  The  stitching 
shall  be  made  by  using  cotton  sewing  thread. 

5  REQUIREMENTS 

5.1  The  general  makeup  of  the  net  shall  be  as 
shown  in  Fig    1 

5.2  Dimensions 

The  nets  shall  conform  to  the  following 
dimensions 

Length,  cm  198      ±  5 

Width,  cm  107     ±  3 

Total  height  (  including  147     ±  4 

bottom      reinforcement 
piece  ) 

Height        of        bottom  28  0  ±  0  5 

reinforcement  piece,  cm 

5.3  Colour/Shade 

The  colour/shade  of  the  nets  shall  be  as  specified 
in  the  contract  or  order  In  case  a  sample  has 
been  agreed  upon  and  sealed  the  supply  shall  be 
made  in  conlormity  with  that  sample  in  such 
respects 

5.4  Joined  Nets 

The  joined  nets  shall  be  permitted  in  maximum 
20  percent  of  the  supply  However,  the  width 
of  the  panel  in  the  joined  net  shall  not  be  less 
than  one  metre

IS  9886  :  1990 


5.5  If  so  specified  in  the  contract  or  order  the 
following  be  provided  in  the  net 

a)  65  mm  wide  cotton  cahco  strengthening 
strips  along  diagonals  at  the  top 

b)  Gathering  be  provided  in  the  walls 
through  additional  15  cm  netting  at  each 
corner  to  ensure  proper  shape,  checking 
shrinkage  and  taking  care  of  the  extra 
stretch  when  turned  in  under  the  bed  or 
mattress 

NOTE — In  case  such  J  5  cm  gathering  is  provided  at 
each  top  corner  the  bottom  parameter  of  the  net  is 
increased  bv  60  cm 

6  MARKING 

6.1  The  following  information  shall  be  indelibly 
marked  on  the  cloth  label  securely  stitched  at 
the  top  corner 

a)  Indication  of  the  source  of  manufacture, 

b)  Size  of  the  net,  namely,  overall  length 
(  cm  )  x  overall  width  (  cm  )  X  overall 
height  (  cm  ) 

c)  Type  of  net, 

d)  Month  and  year  of  manufacture   and 

e)  Any  other  information  mentioned  in 
contract/order/statutory  provisions 

7  PACKING 

7.1  The  mosquito  nets  shall  be  packed  as 
stipulated  in  the  contract/order   a  recommended 


procedure  is  given  below 

Five  nets  suitably  folded  shall  be  placed  one  over 
the  other  and  tied  with  jute  twine  (  see  variety 
No  8  of  IS  1912  1984  )  to  form  a  bundle  Ten 
such  bundles  shall  then  be  wrapped  with  one 
layer  of  polyethylene  film  of  minimum  40  p-m 
thickness  (  see  IS  2508  1984)  followed  by  an 
outer  layer  of  heavy  cee  cloth  {see  IS  2874  1964  ) 
or  hessian  cloth,  305  g/ma  (  see  Type  1  of 
IS  2818  (  Part  2  )  1971  ]  to  form  a  bale  The 
bale  shall  be  stitched  at  the  sides  with  jute  twine 
of  300  tex  X  3  ply  with  not  less  than  12  stitches 
per  dm  The  size  of  the  packing  material  used 
shall  be  sufficiently  large  to  wrap  completely  the 
mosquito  net  bundles  Care  should  be  taken 
while  stitching  the  sides  of  the  bales  so  that  the 
inner  material  does  not  get  pierced 

8  SAMPLING 

8.1  Lot 

The  quantity  of  mosquito  nets  delivered  to  a 
consignee  against  the  same  despatch  note  shall 
constitute  a  lot 

8.2  The  sampling  plan  shall  be  as  specified  in 
the  contract  or  order  Assistance  may  be  derived 
from  IS  2500  (  Part  1  )  1973  in  demising  a  suit- 
able single,  double  or  multiple  sampling  and 
inspection  plan  The  acceptance  quality  level 
(  AQL  )  should  not  exceed  2  5  percent 

8.3  Samples  of  mosquito  nets  shall  be  drawn  at 
random  (  see  IS  4905     1968  )

ANNEX  B 
(  Clause  3-1  ) 

RECOMMENDED  REQUIREMENTS  OF  NYLON  MOSQUITO  NETTING 
(  As  given  in  Provisional  Defence  Specification  IND/TC/0144  ) 


B-l  GENERAL  REQUIREMENTS 

B-l.l  The  netting  shall  be  made  from  polyamide 
multifilament  yarn  (see  IS  667:1981)  of 
40  denier  (  4  4  tex  )  L  10  percent.  The  mesh 
of  the  netting  shall  be  round.

attending  to  connected  matters  in  the  country

Review  of  Indian  Standards 

Amendment  s  are  issued  to  standards  as  the  need  arises  on  the  basis  of  comments  Standards  are  also  reviewed 
periodically,  a  standard  along  with  amendments  is  reaffirmed  when  such  review  indicates  that  no  changes  are 
needed,  if  the  review  indicates  that  changes  arc  needed,  it  is  taken  up  for  revision  Users  of  Indian  Standards 
should  ascertain  that  they  are  in  possession  of  the  latest  amendments  or  edition  by  referring  to  the  latest  issue 
of    BIS  Catalogue'  and  'Standards    Monthly  Additions*
